page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256gb is a memory-optimized server configuration within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include a GPU and relies on 1 GB of network-attached local storage, with one complimentary public IPv4 address included.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with the Passmark memory score and large-block memory write bandwidth both ranking in the top 10% tier. Single-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests, while multi-core CPU performance is average, landing in the middle 50%. The server excels in data decompression and compression, with single-threaded gzip and bzip3 speeds reaching the top 10% tier. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput all register in the top 25% tier.

Operating on a shared CPU allocation, this instance offers a cost-effective profile for memory-heavy workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU execution. The primary hardware tradeoff is the minimal 1 GB of network storage, meaning users must provision external storage for data-intensive setups. Given its high memory bandwidth and capacity, this server is well-suited for large-scale caching, database hosting, memory-intensive web serving, and moderate language model inference.
